Lemma
[Polar Form of the Euclidean Metric] ↗ ex:warped-products ↗ prop:warped-product-isometry ↗ UNRESOLVED:chA:2-4 1. ch10:10.13

On $\mathbb R^n\setminus \{ 0\} $, the Euclidean metric $\bar g$ satisfies \begin{equation} \bar g=dr^2+r^2\hat g. \quad (10.15) \end{equation} where $r(x)=|x|$.

Proof

\sketch The map

\begin{equation} \Phi (\rho ,\omega )=\rho \omega \quad (10.16) \end{equation}

is an isometry from the warped product $\mathbb R^+\times _\rho S^{n-1}$ with metric $d\rho ^2\oplus \rho ^2\check g$ to Euclidean space minus the origin. Since $\Phi ^{-1}(x)=(r(x),\pi (x))$, pulling back this identity gives (10.15).

□
